register.labelZh: HAVE 片語動詞的實際用途
register.summaryZh: have somebody in 可以表示安排工人到來工作;have somebody over 則表示邀請客人到家中作客。；你可以用 have somebody down as 表示對某人的看法,也可以用 have somebody on 表示哄騙或戲弄某人。；have something in 可以表示備有物資;have something back 表示取回物品;have something out則表示把某物移除。；have something against somebody 表示對某人有不滿;have somebody up 則表示起訴某人。；have it off 和 have it away 可能出現在英國電影、娛樂新聞和成人之間的非正式對話中。懂得它們的意思並不代表你必須親自使用。
register.summaryEn: Have somebody in can describe arranging for workers to come, while have somebody over describes inviting guests to your home. You can have somebody down as a particular type of person or have somebody on by making them believe something untrue. Have something in describes available supplies, have something back describes receiving something again, and have something out describes removal. Have something against somebody describes a negative feeling, while have somebody up describes taking legal action against a person. Have it off and have it away may appear in British films, gossip and informal adult conversations. Understanding them does not mean that you need to use them yourself.
